profile.name: Matthew De Jesus
profile.title: Power Electronics & Hardware Engineer
profile.tagline: MIT MEng candidate in EECS, background in power electronics, analog IC design, and embedded systems.
about: Master of Engineering candidate at MIT previously working in the Research Laboratory of Electronics, where I designed high-frequency PCB test platforms to characterize loss mechanisms in next-generation GaN power transistors. My work spans the full hardware stack, analog integrated circuit design to embedded software.

I like building solutions to problems where physics, circuits, and software meet. It's resulted in a Python design sweep optimizing a synchronous buck converter to 97.8% efficiency, taping out a CMOS amplifier in Intel's 22nm process, pipelining a RISC-V CPU, and creating a custom dashboard for lab measurements. I care about hands-on work, learning by doing, and building things that work in the real world.
